Codex PASS lacked valid task or source evidence for every premise. PASS applies only to restricted A–H. The original INCONCLUSIVE report remains unchanged as an assessment of original S10. The separating singularity-class topology and unrestricted P01/P17 connection remain open.

I independently checked the supplied current43ebad proof, all four author supplements, the original report, and every complete note n1–n10. Prior verdicts, hashes, candidate flags, compilation receipts and reported symbolic tests were not mathematical premises. All indispensable imported foundations are expressly permitted task background, hence excluded from premises. Passage index −1 identifies that background; premises=[] does not claim an elementary self-contained proof.

I opened the matching primary sources: [Bedford–Taylor](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf), [BGL](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.01090), [Darvas v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.7318v3), and [Berndtsson](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1103.0923). The seven original foundation statements have their asserted scope in the complete primary contexts. BT Theorem 2.1/Corollary 2.2 supply bounded decreasing continuity and the positive closed symmetric multilinear pairing. BGL §2.1 supplies the bounded smooth-correction construction, locality, restriction compatibility and positivity without BMP. Darvas supplies closed-base completion, rooftops, endpoint convergence, full-mass projection, bounded Dirichlet uniqueness and the smooth-endpoint distance formula. Its operator is i∂∂̄ and its norm is unnormalized. Berndtsson’s cited construction concerns bounded line-bundle metrics and supports the projective application. Darvas’s inherited Calabi–Chen NPC, closed energy and uniqueness dependencies, and BGL’s inherited local Bedford–Taylor foundations retain their disclosed nonrecursive boundary.

The historical binding map [0,1,1,2,3,4,5,5,6] is preserved. Original passage 2 quotes BGL’s BMP assumption for the different global §2.2. It remains a boundary warning and is excluded from positive evidence for original premise 1. The remaining eight applications were independently checked using their complete contexts; their short snippets alone do not certify every hypothesis.

The actual support DAG is acyclic: n1←[]; n2←[n1]; n3←[n1,n2]; n4←[n1,n2,n3]; n5←[n1,n2,n3,n4]; n6←[n1,n2,n3,n4,n5]; n7←[n1,n2,n3,n4,n5]; n8←[n1,n2,n3,n4,n7]; n9←[n1,n2,n3,n4,n5]; n10←[n1,…,n9]. No target conclusion is imported as a foundation. The forward explanatory reference from n4 to n7 does not provide circular support for completion.

A / n2. The deck action is free and properly discontinuous. Writing z=e^xw with ||w||=1 identifies the quotient smoothly with S^(2n−1)×S¹; the compact radial fundamental annulus proves compactness. Projective charts give the holomorphic submersion with fiber C*/e^Z. Scalar multiplication has kernel Z+2πiZ and gives the transitive elliptic action. Intermediate positive even real cohomology of X vanishes. A product of positive-dimensional compact complex manifolds has a nonzero pullback of a factor’s oriented top class in such a degree, because projection has a smooth section. Thus X admits no such product decomposition.

Set r=log||z||² and α=dd^cr=π*κ. With the specified operator, β=i∂r∧∂̄r/(2π). Scalar multiplication shifts r by a constant, so α, β and h descend and are E-invariant. The kernel of α is the vertical complex line, where β is positive, proving that h is Hermitian. Direct differentiation gives dβ=−dr∧α and dd^cβ=−α², hence dh≠0. On a fiber, r=2x+constant and d^cr=dy/(2π); β=dx∧dy/π with periods 1 and 2π. Therefore ∫Eβ=2. Since β²=0 and α^n=0, h^n=nβ∧α^d and ∫Xh^n=2n. Also dd^c(h^k)=−kα^(k+1), so dd^c(h^d)=0. The background is big with ρ=0 and ε=1.

For current positivity, write the total current locally as π*T+β, where T=pr_Y*κ+dd^cV. The vertical coefficient r_w is nonzero. Every smooth base-and-strip (1,0) vector ξ has a unique lift ξ−∂r(ξ)∂w/r_w annihilating ∂r. Contracting the positive total current with these smooth lifts eliminates β. Testing with nonnegative compact fiber densities gives positivity of T as a distribution on the base. Conversely positive T pulls back positively and β can be added. This never restricts a singular current to a fiber. An invariant potential descends as a locally integrable distribution; canonical recovery or local holomorphic sections recovers its genuine base representative. Canonical equality holds everywhere, including poles. The same argument applies on strips.

B / n3. For bounded v, local decreasing smooth psh approximations and the bounded smooth-correction polynomial give the actual identity (h+dd^cπ*v)^n=nβ∧π*(κ+dd^cv)^d. All other terms vanish by horizontal degree or β²=0. For general v use v_j=max(v,−j). Exactly, π*v_j=max(π*v,−j), including pole values. Thus locality gives the same identity after multiplying by the genuine strict superlevel indicator. The closed-base finite-level measures increase and have mass at most one; the Hopf measures consequently increase with mass at most 2n. Their limit is the actual finite non-pluripolar measure nβ∧π*MAκ(v). Each finite level vanishes on every pluripolar set, and an increasing setwise limit retains that property. No pole-set wedge, arbitrary rough-current pullback or Hopf BMP theorem is used. The measure β∧π*μ is concretely defined by fiber integration against μ. Tonelli proves the asserted 2n integration factor for every nonnegative Borel F, including infinite integrals.

Every full Perron competitor is convex in real time at each fixed spatial point, allowing the identically −∞ restriction. Consequently W_t≤(1−t)π*v_0+tπ*v_1. The full family is locally uniformly bounded above and is permuted by E. A pulled-back base competitor supplies nontriviality. Its canonical envelope is therefore invariant and descends by A. The chord bound survives usc regularization and preserves the original joint boundary upper bounds, including poles, by endpoint usc and the finite upper bounds of the other endpoint. Its descent is a base competitor; conversely every base competitor pulls back. These inclusions prove equality of the full envelopes. Open submersion charts ensure commutation with usc regularization. The chord argument also reconciles the printed temporal boundary convention with the original joint convention.

For E² endpoints, their E² rooftop supplies a nontrivial constant-in-time competitor. Closed-base capacity and L¹ endpoint convergence applies. The exact identity ∫X|π*(v_t−v_i)|h^n/(2n)=∫Y|v_t−v_i|κ^d transfers L¹ convergence. Every prescribed smooth positive probability dV has bounded positive density ratio with h^n/(2n) on compact X, so convergence holds for the original dV and canonical endpoints. No product-capacity claim is needed.

C / n4. Smooth basic positive potentials and paths correspond bijectively to smooth positive base potentials and paths. The actual measure identity gives G_X(π*ξ,π*η)=2n∫Yξη(κ+dd^cv)^d. Setting f=v/(2π) leaves the current unchanged, while tangents gain the factor 2π. Squared norms therefore gain (2π)²·2n and lengths gain 2π√(2n). Taking the same smooth basic path infima gives exactly the stated distance conversion. The permitted closed-base completion transfers through this scaled bijection to precisely the genuine basic full-mass finite-second-moment potentials; B proves the equivalent actual Hopf characterization. Completeness and unique constant-speed geodesics transfer, and B identifies those geodesics with the full Hermitian Perron segments. Smooth constant translations have base distance |c|, and approximation extends this to the completion, giving d_B(u,u+c)=√(2n)|c|. Nonbasic paths never enter this distance definition.

D / n5. Endpoint distance is at most metric length; Cauchy–Schwarz gives A_B≥d_B(p,q)²/2. Equality forces constant speed and length equal to distance. Subinterval length bounds and the endpoint triangle inequality then force the metric-segment identity on every subinterval. Unique geodesics give the unique minimizer, including the constant curve when endpoints agree.

For smooth speed, put Δ=v_{s+δ}−v_s. C¹ dependence in spatial C² gives Δ=O(δ), Δ/δ→dot v_s and time remainder o(δ). The auxiliary chord has uniformly positive spatial form and mixed strip coefficients O(δ). Subtracting Kδ²τ(1−τ), with sufficiently large uniform K, makes its temporal coefficient dominate the squared mixed Schur complement. It is a subgeodesic with exact endpoints. Hence its Perron segment G satisfies chord−Kδ²τ(1−τ)≤G≤chord and Δ−Kδ²≤dot G_0≤Δ. Formula (15), applied only at these smooth endpoints and converted by f=v/(2π), yields the raw squared base speed after division by δ². Multiplication by 2n gives the Hopf speed. Smooth path-length bounds give absolute continuity, so integration proves A_B=S_X. This does not use a singular initial-velocity formula.

For all-variation stationarity, differentiate the original full action: L(w)=∫[dot u·dot w·ω_u^n+(n/2)dot u²dd^cw∧ω_u^(n−1)]dt. The action is E-invariant and the central basic path is E-fixed, so its continuous linear differential satisfies L(w)=L(∫E g*w dg). The average is smooth basic with zero endpoints. Uniform positivity makes every smooth direction admissible for sufficiently small parameter. Before differentiating, the basic action is exactly 2n times the closed-base action. With η=κ+dd^cv and f=dot v, actual integration by parts gives L_Y(q)=∫q[−ddot v·η^d+d·df∧d^cf∧η^(d−1)]dt. The identity dd^c(f²)=2fdd^cf+2df∧d^cf cancels the mixed terms; the smooth base HCMA Schur complement makes the remaining bracket zero with the stated operator. Thus every full-X first variation vanishes. Torsion was retained in the full differential. Only basic-domain minimization is asserted.

E / n6. The projective ratio is globally smooth. The holomorphic map F([z],s)=[e^(a_js/2)z_j] gives pr_Y*κ+dd^cV=F*κ, of rank d, with strictly positive spatial slices and zero (d+1)st power. Bounded closed-base Dirichlet uniqueness identifies the base Perron segment; B and D give the full Hopf segment and all-variation stationarity. Changing variables by F_t makes its squared base velocity constant. Uniform simplex moments are 2/[n(n+1)] on the diagonal and 1/[n(n+1)] off it. Therefore its squared base speed is [(Σa_j)²+Σa_j²]/[n(n+1)]. Multiplying by 2n gives the stated squared distance; action is half that number. The threefold specialization gives 1 and 1/2. Unequal a_j give different values ta_j at coordinate points for t>0, proving spatial nonconstancy.

F / n7. For each finite C, the full envelope below 0 and π*v+C is nonempty, uniformly bounded above and E-invariant. It remains below the usc obstacles and descends by A, while every base obstacle competitor pulls back. Taking the increasing union over C and canonical usc regularization proves P_h[π*v]=π*Pκ[v]. This proves the model embedding without incorrectly treating the final projection as a same-type competitor. The closed-base full-mass projection theorem with zero obstacle sends every E² point to zero. Thus all B₂ points project to zero although their metric distinguishes points and constants. It cannot descend through that projection or ordinary equivalence. Affine maximum barriers and the chord bound retain the common ordinary type for equivalent endpoints. None of this computes extrema of mass over the full Hopf ordinary type.

Both pointwise Legendre operations commute with pullback, and open submersions commute with usc regularization. Model normalization, concavity, monotonicity and poles are preserved. Under the explicit antecedent that the associated base Perron ray has every finite slice in E², each finite restriction falls under B–D. Its native minimum action on an interval of duration T−s is d_B(u_s,u_T)²/[2(T−s)], or d_B²/2 after unit-interval rescaling. The finite-energy antecedent is retained; no unrestricted stretching or singularity-topology conclusion follows.

G / n8. In the affine chart let s=log|w|², L=log(1+e^s), p=e^s/(1+e^s), q=1+L−s and H=L+1−q^a. Its slope is A=p+a(1−p)q^(a−1)>0, with A'=p(1−p)(1−a q^(a−1))+a(1−a)(1−p)²q^(a−2)>0. These prove radial Levi positivity. The homogeneous formula is smooth across infinity and equals zero there. Canonical cutoffs have local psh potentials max(H,L−j), equal to L−j near o. They decrease to the genuine nontrivial κ-psh potential with value −∞ at o; logarithmic growth against exponential radial volume gives local integrability.

The exact determinant is (dd^cH)^d=(d!/π^d)A^(d−1)A'|w|^(−2d)dλ. Sphere area 2π^d/(d−1)! and ds=2dR/R give radial measure dA^(d−1)A'ds times normalized angular measure. Equivalently d^cs has Hopf-circle integral one and dd^cs induces mass-one Fubini–Study on P^(d−1). Thus annular flux is exactly A^d. In q coordinates, p=e^(1−q), and A decreases from one to zero. At canonical level j the strict superlevel is q<Q_j=(1+j)^(1/a), excluding the inner constant region and any cutoff shell. Its actual finite-level mass is exactly 1−A(Q_j)^d. The smooth hyperplane at infinity has zero measure. Increasing levels give actual full mass one with no pole atom.

The exact squared moment integrates (q^a−1)²dA(q)^(d−1)[p(1−a q^(a−1))+a(1−a)(1−p)q^(a−2)]dq from one to infinity. Its tail density is asymptotic to d a^d(1−a)q^((d+2)a−d−1). It is finite exactly when a<d/(d+2). At equality its truncation at Q is d a^d(1−a)log Q+O(1), because the residual power corrections are integrable and exponential corrections negligible. B supplies precisely the Hopf factor 2n for mass and energy. The genuine pole is the whole fiber over o. For a<b, v_b≤v_a but v_a−v_b=q^b−q^a→∞, so mutual ordinary order fails. Subcritical distinct points have finite positive distance and identical zero model projections.

H / n9. The radius is globally defined modulo two, so all displayed periodic paths descend. Spatial differentiation gives h+dd^cu=(1+u_r)α+(1+u_rr)β. Fiber integration gives the exact action n∫〈u_t²(1+u_r)^d(1+u_rr)〉dt. Convexity bounds every full strip competitor from 0 to c by ct, which is itself a competitor. The full first variation at ct is c∫w_t h^n+(nc²/2)∫dd^cw∧h^d; endpoints and dd^c(h^d)=0 eliminate both terms for arbitrary full-X variations.

The full Hessian is ∫[w_t²h^n+2ncw_tdd^cw∧h^d+(ndc²/2)(dd^cw)²∧h^(d−1)]dt. For radial endpoint-zero directions, periodic integration eliminates the w_rw_rr term, while ∫〈w_tw_rr〉dt=−[〈w_r²〉]₀¹/2=0. It reduces exactly to Q(w)=2n∫〈(w_t+dcw_r)²−d(d+1)c²w_r²/2〉dt. For w_k=sin(πt)cos(πk(r−dct)), Q(w_k)=nπ²[1−d(d+1)c²k²/2]/2. Distinct positive integer modes are orthogonal. The algebraic span of sufficiently large modes is an infinite-dimensional negative subspace. Each finite combination admits arbitrarily small positive spatial variations, and a negative direction lowers action near the stationary path.

For the explicit threefold competitor, positivity follows from 1−π|ε| and 1−π²|ε|, both positive at ε=1/100. Independent periodic expansion gives quadratic coefficient p²/2−3π²f²/2−π²fp and quartic coefficient π²f²p²/8+3π⁴f³p/4+3π⁴f⁴/2, where f=sin(πt), p=f'. Their time integrals are −π²/2 and 37π⁴/64; odd powers vanish by the circle half-turn. Multiplication by three proves the exact polynomial 3−3π²ε²/2+111π⁴ε⁴/64. It is below three for 0<ε²<32/(37π²), including ε=1/100, where it is approximately 2.998521248778759. For every c≠0, a sufficiently small negative-direction variation has action below nc². Cauchy–Schwarz gives L_raw²≤2S_X<2nc² and the asserted strict length comparison. These competitors need not be subgeodesics. No full-infimum metric definiteness or completion is inferred.

Corrections and comparison. The four disclosed source changes preserve the targets: bounded BGL scope and separate truncation construction, the cohomological nonproduct argument, arbitrary-dV endpoint passage, and BT 1987 fine-topology attribution. The older b₁ comparison alone excluded Y×E, not all product decompositions; the current proof establishes the stronger target. The older private C¹ claim needs o(δ), rather than an O(δ²) time remainder; current43ebad and n5 correctly make this distinction. A harmless n1 attribution clarification is also needed: mean-zero is an optional Green-function normalization, not explicitly imposed in printed Darvas §7. The unit-Dirac equation requires curve volume one; at volume V its right side is Vδ_o. The printed singular-velocity counterexample is unchanged, and A–H never use that illustrative coefficient. No substantial repair of restricted A–H is needed.

The n10 scope conclusion is justified: this is substantive nonclosed, nonproduct potential-space progress with a complete basic metric, coherent metric-speed action, full Perron compatibility, all-variation smooth stationarity, nonconstant examples and genuine singular examples. Its complete topology concerns potentials with constants retained. Projection collapse and positive constant distances prevent inference of a separating singularity-class metric. It does not complete original S10/P01/P17.
